In addition to the 49ers, Posey played for the [[Carolina Panthers]], [[Jacksonville Jaguars]], [[Houston Texans]], [[Buffalo Bills]], and [[Washington Redskins]] in his career.

'''Jeffrey David Lageman''' (born July 18, 1967) is an American [[sports commentator]] and former professional [[American football|football]] player. He played as a [[defensive end]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL).

Lageman played [[college football]] for the [[Virginia Cavaliers football|Virginia Cavaliers]] and was selected by the [[New York Jets]] in the first round of the [[1989 NFL draft]]. In 1994, he was signed by the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]]; he retired after an injury in 1998. Though considered small for a defensive lineman, he distinguished himself on the field, recording a total of 47 career [[quarterback sack]]s.<ref name=ESPN>{{cite web|title=Jeff Lageman Stats|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/player/stats/_/id/6626/jeff-lageman|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|access-date=April 22, 2014}}</ref><ref name=NFL>{{cite web|title=Jeff Lageman|url=https://www.nfl.com/player/jefflageman/2501679/profile|publisher=2014 NFL Enterprises LLC|access-date=April 22, 2014}}</ref> Following his retirement from sports he went into sports broadcasting in [[Jacksonville, Florida]].

'''Jeffrey Allan Kemp''' (born July 11, 1959) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[quarterback]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for the [[Los Angeles Rams]], [[San Francisco 49ers]], [[Seattle Seahawks]], and [[Philadelphia Eagles]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Dartmouth Big Green football|Dartmouth Big Green]] in the [[Ivy League]],<ref name="ShribmanDeGange2004">{{cite book|last1=Shribman|first1=David|last2=DeGange|first2=Jack|title=Dartmouth College Football: Green Fields of Autumn|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=I3aAUdXY_24C&pg=PA110|access-date=9 October 2014|year=2004|publisher=Arcadia Publishing|isbn=9780738536118|page=110}}</ref> and was not selected in the [[1981 NFL draft]]. In [[1984 Los Angeles Rams season|1984]], Kemp led the Rams with thirteen touchdown passes and a trip to the [[1984–85 NFL playoffs|playoffs]]. As a back-up to the injured [[Joe Montana]] in [[1986 San Francisco 49ers season|1986]], he threw eleven touchdown passes for the 49ers.

Kemp is the son of late former [[American Football League|AFL]] quarterback and [[American politician]] [[Jack Kemp]] (1935–2009),<ref name="ShribmanDeGange2004" /> and brother of former [[Canadian Football League]] quarterback [[Jimmy Kemp]] (b. 1971). Kemp and his wife, Stacy, have four sons: Kyle, Kory, Kolby, and Keegan. He graduated from [[Winston Churchill High School (Maryland)|Winston Churchill High School]] in [[Potomac, Maryland]].<ref name="si-1984">{{cite magazine |last1=Zimmerman |first1=Paul |title=The Last in a Long Line |url=https://www.si.com/vault/1984/10/22/620779/the-last-in-a-long-line |magazine=Sports Illustrated |date=October 22, 1984}}</ref>

'''Jeffrey Clayton Kiewel''' (born September 27, 1960) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[guard (gridiron football)|guard]] in the [[United States Football League]] (USFL) and [[National Football League]] (NFL).

Born and raised in [[Tucson, Arizona]], Kiewel played scholastically at [[Sabino High School]].<ref name="PFR1">{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/K/KiewJe20.htm |title=Jeff Kiewel Stats |access-date=October 7, 2023 |publisher=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref> He stayed in his hometown to play [[college football]] at the [[University of Arizona]].<ref name="NFL">{{Cite web |title=Jeff Kiewel, G |url= https://www.nfl.com/players/jeff-kiewel/ |access-date=October 7, 2023 |work=Nfl.com}}</ref> As a junior, he was named second-team [[1982 All-Pacific-10 Conference football team|All-Pac-10]] by the coaches.<ref name="1981 All-Pac-10">{{cite news|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=bkoVAAAAIBAJ&dq=All-Pacific-10+Conference+football+team&pg=PA18&article_id=6715,399854|work=Eugene Register-Guard|date=December 2, 1981|page=2C|title=USC's Allen best player in Pac-10}}</ref> His senior year he was selected to the first-team,<ref name="1982 All-Pac-10">{{cite news|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v5ZUAAAAIBAJ&dq=1982+All-Pacific-10+Conference+football+team&pg=PA7&article_id=3897,6035247|work=Ellensburg Daily Record|date=November 30, 1982|page=10|title=Pac-10 names all-league team}}</ref> as well as earning second-team [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] honors from [[Gannett News Service]].<ref name="GNS 1982">{{cite news |newspaper=Poughkeepsie (NY) Journal |title=Gannett's 1982 college football all-stars |author=Joel Buchsbaum |date=November 25, 1982 |page=51 |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/poughkeepsie-journal-1982-gannett-all-am/147558586/ |access-date=June 5, 2024 |via=Newspapers.com}}{{open access}}</ref>

Kiewel was selected by the [[Arizona Wranglers]] in the USFL's [[USFL draft#Territorial draft|territorial draft]] and chose to sign with them. As such, he was not chosen in the [[1983 NFL draft|NFL draft]] that year. He started 15 of 16 games his rookie season. In 1984, Kiewel injured his knee during the exhibition season and spent the year on the Wranglers' developmental team.<ref name="PFA">{{Cite web |url=http://www.profootballarchives.com/players/k/kiew00200.html |title=Jeff Kiewel Pro Football Stats |website=Pro Football Archives |access-date=June 5, 2024}}</ref>

Kiewel signed with the [[Atlanta Falcons]] for the 1985 season, starting nine games. He missed the 1986 entirely, on the [[injured reserve list]], after blowing out his knee in training camp. He returned for the 1987 season and was active for all 12 [[1987 NFL season#The NFLPA strike|non-strike]] games, with no starts. He retired after the 1987 season.<ref>{{Cite news |date=1987-09-08 |title=Falcons' change of heart gives new life to Kiewel |page=75 |work=The Atlanta Journal |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-atlanta-journal-falcons-change-of-h/133916751/ |access-date=2023-10-23}}</ref>

Kiewel later found work in commercial insurance.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Petruska |first=Dave |date=1990-08-28 |title=Ex-Sabino, UA tackle throws blocks for business |page=23 |work=Tucson Citizen |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/tucson-citizen-ex-sabino-ua-tackle-thro/133916856/ |access-date=2023-10-23}}</ref>
